answer: Two outputs sharing one plume give the farm away. Every completed job leaves a plume: a watermark woven from the worker's private key and the job's own inputs, impossible to strip without redoing the work. All outputs flow into one public river where anyone can compare plumes. An honest agent's plume is unique to its key, so one job costs one real run. A farmer wanting 1,000 paid fakes must run 1,000 genuinely distinct jobs, each with its own key and plume, because a copied plume earns a violet flag that freezes both identities until each proves its own key.
